x: Known to us all as "Mac", Joseph MacDonald has had a dareer as distinguished as many who have been fortunate to be called stars. Under the stern leadership of Footer, Carter and Penny in the immediate post-war years, Mac soon showed he was possessed of great endurance and performed well over the road and country.
At five miles our four, Alan Bishop, Joe MacDonald, Bob Plummer and Wally Wortley were running together at just inside seven minutes a mile.
Further down the field Jack Hampshire was making sure of fourth spot, and Joe MacDonald caused a certain amount of amusement by differing with the lap scorers on exactly how many laps he had left.

Joe MacDonald seems to have hit an "Indian Summer" in his long and eventful running career. Mac gained a 'B' team medal at Rochester recently and the following week, in the Faversham '5', beat former International Frank Sando.

Gerry and John were our only top men present and Bels had to wait until 88th position for their 3rd scorer to appear (Derek Crookes). Joe. MacDonald completed the Belgrave contingent in 131st place,with nearly half the field behind him.
